required_actions: Open an existing conversation with the recipient or start a new one (critical)
Tap Wi-Fi and turn Wi-Fi on (critical)
Confirm the blue tick next to the network name and the Wi-Fi icon at the top (confirmation)
Open Settings from the Start button (critical)
Under Scale & layout, open the Scale dropdown (critical)
Follow the on-screen prompts to set the new password (critical)
Choose Remove Other Devices or Keep All Devices Signed In if asked (non-critical)
Note that you might have to wait one hour before changing the password (non-critical)
Click the Attach icon at the bottom of the compose window (critical)
Note the 25 MB limit and the Google Drive link for larger attachments (non-critical)
Open the Settings app and tap your name (critical)
Open the Photos app and tap Library to see the photos in iCloud (critical final check)
unsupported_claims: 'Your photos will start saving to iCloud on their own.' -> the cited page says photos 'are added to iCloud' once sync is on; it never says the upload is automatic and gives no timing.
'so they're safe even if the phone is lost or broken' -> the page says nothing about loss, damage, or protection, and it never describes iCloud Photos as a backup, which is what the user asked about.
reasons: Round 3 is the last allowed re-review. The steps are correct, but the reply makes two protection and automatic-saving claims the cited iCloud Photos page does not support (G1 fails). Two earlier rounds did not remove them, so the example is rejected. The page also describes iCloud Photos sync, not a backup, so a new example would need a source that covers backup.
fix: Not re-reviewable in this batch. For the Data Lead: if the example is rewritten, delete 'so they're safe even if the phone is lost or broken' and replace 'on their own' with 'Once sync is on, the photos and videos in your Photos app are added to iCloud.' Keep the five steps and the Library line. Do not present iCloud Photos as a backup unless a source for backup is added.
